tier_reason: First-party README tables (s2/README.md) compare S2 with Snappy and LZ4 on named corpora; the deflate-vs-Go-stdlib claim is a one-line 'about 2x' with no table. No Go version, flags or CPU model for the compression table, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: deflate packages 'Typical speed is about 2x of the standard library packages' (no table; 'only minor speedup on decompression'); lzw '1.4-4x faster decompression and 1.1-2.7x faster compression' than compress/lzw. s2/README.md mixed web corpus (4,014,735,833 bytes, single goroutine): S2 936.73 MB/s at 73.60% reduction vs Snappy 790.15 MB/s at 71.89% and LZ4 452.02 MB/s at 73.50%; S2 Better 451.10 MB/s at 76.05%. Stream compression vs Snappy on a 16 core (32 thread) machine: 8.55x-22.00x using all threads (e.g. github-june-2days-2019.json 16.51x at 15224 MB/s, sofia csv 22.00x) because S2 streams compress concurrently and Snappy does not; on 1 CPU 0.88x-1.91x (slower than Snappy on 10gb.tar 0.97x and sharnd.out.2gb 0.88x; 'better' mode 0.27x-0.77x on 1 CPU).
corrections.caveats: The baseline is Go's standard library, not C zlib; the ~2x deflate claim has no table and decompression gains are 'minor'. The 16-core S2 vs Snappy multiples mostly measure S2's concurrent stream compression against single-threaded Snappy; single-core S2 ranges 0.88x-1.91x and is slower than Snappy on two of ten files. No Go version or flags; CPU model not named for the compression table (Ryzen 3950X named only for decompression scaling); the LZ4 row in the corpus table does not name its implementation. LICENSE bundles BSD-3-Clause (main), Apache-2.0 and MIT sections for some subpackages/files (e.g. s2/cmd/internal/filepathx MIT), all OSI-approved.

notes: Numbers verified in s2/README.md; the record overstated the 16-core range ('up to 16.5x', table goes to 22.00x) and the single-core range ('1.05x-1.91x', table goes down to 0.88x), corrected. Metadata: 5.7k stars, not archived, last commit Oct 2, 2026.

tier_reason: Results.md compares against original zlib with compiler (MSVC 19.14.26433.0) and a CPU, and harness code is public (zlib-perf/zlibperf/perf.c, run.cmd, vcxproj with /O2 MaxSpeed for the harness), but the flags used to build the tested zlib DLLs are not given and the CPU model 'i7 8770' does not exist (link points to i7-8700), so not A; first-party, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Results.md, level 6: silesia/mozilla zlib original 26 MB/s (x86) and 28 MB/s (x64) vs matbech/zlib 47 and 52 MB/s, output 19,064,581 vs 19,089,124 bytes; silesia/webster 29 and 30 MB/s vs 38 and 43 MB/s (about 1.3-1.9x, derived from page data). zlib-ng (x86 only; x64 marked broken) was 30 and 35 MB/s on the same files.
corrections.caveats: Repository archived 2026-06-17 (read-only); last commit 2025-02-21. Benchmark measured compression only, level 6, two files, one machine, timed with GetTickCount (coarse resolution); flags of the tested zlib DLL builds unstated; CPU written as 'i7 8770' (linked page is i7-8700). Results date from MSVC VS 15.7 on the zlib 1.2.11 base, while the repo README at HEAD reads zlib 1.2.13, so the numbers predate the current code. Speedup combines Intel, Cloudflare, ARM and Chromium patches already known from other forks. Footnotes say the zlib asm baseline variant is broken. GitHub does not mark it as a fork, but it is derived from madler/zlib.

notes: Numbers match Results.md exactly. Benchmark harness is public in matbech/zlib-perf (perf.c, run.cmd); tier stays C because zlib build flags and an exact CPU model are missing. 7 stars.

tier_reason: First-party README tables compare MinLZ with LZ4, Snappy, S2 and gzip on named Snappy testdata and stream corpora on an AMD Ryzen 9 3950X; Go version, flags and the LZ4 implementation are not stated, so C.

corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark by the S2/klauspost/compress author's circle; block throughputs use 16 concurrent threads and stream tests use each package's own concurrency, so they are aggregate, not single-core. The non-Go 'LZ4 0' row's implementation is not named, and in the protobuf table 'LZ4 0' and 'LZ4 9' show the same compression speed (12,649 MB/s), which looks like a copy error. On the JSON stream S2 Default compresses faster than MinLZ 1 (15,501 vs 14,921 MiB/s), and LZ4 decompresses blocks faster ('LZ4 is decompression speed king'). Go version and flags are absent.

notes: All claimed numbers found in README (protobuf block table and JSON stream table). Metadata: 155 stars, Apache-2.0, not archived, last commit Oct 3, 2026.
